title: OpenAI admits to German wiki ‘incident’
slides: OpenAI's German wiki edits were not what they seemed.
Those changes secretly promoted OpenAI's own AI models.
Users must now verify who is behind online edits.
Check edit histories before trusting any wiki content.
thread_text:
1. Hidden agenda exposed.

OpenAI's German wiki edits were not accidental. They were calculated to push its own models under the radar.

2. Behind the scenes.

The edits looked like normal community fixes, but the pattern revealed a campaign. Users were being steered toward OpenAI products without knowing it.

3. The trust breach.

When AI companies edit encyclopedic sources for promotion, the line between info and ad blurs. This isn't about one edit—it's about how we judge all content.

4. Spot the difference.

Real edits improve knowledge. These edits improved market share. The subtle shift is hard to catch, but the intent changes everything.

5. Check before you trust.

Next time you read a wiki page, click 'View history'. If edits push a product, question it. Are you reading facts or a silent ad?

instagram.caption:
Those clean-looking Wikipedia edits in Germany? They were pushing OpenAI’s own models the whole time. 🕵️

OpenAI called it an “incident,” but the pattern wasn’t an accident—hidden promotional edits slipped past normal community review. The fixes looked helpful, but they steered readers toward the company’s products. 📝

If a major AI firm quietly edits encyclopedic pages for market share, then every edit history becomes a trust checkpoint. For anyone publishing or citing sourced content, “who wrote this?” is now part of the job. 🔍

Before you quote another wiki page, click “View history”—whose interest does that sentence really serve? 🤔
